title: An outage drives learners away
description: About a month before the start date, the lessons stop working for nine days: opening a lesson fails with an error, learners reload a few times and give up. When lessons work again, more than half of the learners who ran into the errors never open a lesson again, although they still sign in. Some of them cancel in the following weeks.
expected_finding: Lesson use fell by about a third, and the agent says why: the application was failing during those nine days. It reports a falling trend caused by an outage (a reliability problem), and it withdraws the 'fewer returning learners' finding instead of presenting the fall as learners losing interest.

verified_against.threshold: the outage covers days -32..-24, so it falls in BOTH 30-day windows the agent reads (days -59..-30 and -29..0). The server-error share over the learning routes is about 7-9% in the earlier window and about 28% in the recent one (about 5.6-7.5% and 21% even if the catalog routes were in the same capability), above INCIDENT_ERROR_RATE_PCT = 5, so incident_or_outage is 'confirmed' whichever window the agent read last (checked for start dates on all seven weekdays)

distinct users on /api/lessons/{lessonId}/progress fall about 43-48% between the two windows (quiz route about 55%), above ACTOR_INACTIVITY_DROP_PCT = 33 with about 340 people in the earlier window (MIN_INACTIVITY_ACTORS = 200): an NBF-USAGE-ACTOR_INACTIVITY candidate is built and then withdrawn by SUPPRESSING_CAUSES (incident_or_outage), listed in the detection report as 'explained_by_confirmed_alternative'

daily requests on the learning routes fall about 34-39% between the two halves of the history, beyond TREND_NEGATIVE_PCT = 10, so NBF-DRIFT-GOAL_TREND_NEGATIVE is raised on the goal the lessons serve with the confirmed outage as its cause (DETERMINISTIC_CAUSE_KINDS: no model is asked)
